newsitem.title: UK: Blair says minimum wage won't cost jobs.
newsitem.headline: Blair says minimum wage won't cost jobs.

text.p: British Prime Minister Tony Blair said on Wednesday he did not believe the introduction of a national minimum wage would cost jobs.
Britain's new Labour government plans to introduce a minimum wage after hearing recommendations from a new Low Pay Commission made up of business and trade union representatives.
"I don't believe that a minimum wage is going to increase unemployment at all," Blair told the House of Commons.
"I say that it is wrong, simply wrong, that 800,000 people in this country are paid 2.50 pounds an hour."
Labour politicians have given no indication of what they consider an appropriate level for a minimum wage.
Unions have proposed that it should be at least four pounds per hour, which is nearly half median male earnings, but many employers say this would be too high and would lead to job cuts.
